description: Machine-friendly NL2SQL guide for the M1 master-data module. Covers main tables, business synonyms, join hints, reference relations, and query-generation rules.

join_hints.name: contact_commercial_hierarchy
join_hints.description: Relationship from contacts to categories and assigned salespeople.

join_hints.name: item_classification_flow
join_hints.description: Relationship from items to classifications and commercial attributes.

join_hints.name: warehouse_organization_flow
join_hints.description: Relationship from warehouses to organizational structure and location.

join_hints.name: coa_reference_flow
join_hints.description: Relationship from accounts to parent accounts and organizational dimensions.

join_hints.name: transaction_note_flow
join_hints.description: Relationship from transaction-note headers to note details by source.

important_rules: Use `m1_contact` for questions about customers, suppliers, salespeople, or business-contact relationships.
Use `m1_item` for questions about items, products, item setup, and item classification.
Use `m1_coa` for questions about accounts, parent accounts, opening balances, and account organization dimensions.
Use `m1_warehouse`, `m1_location`, `m1_branch`, and `m1_division` for warehouse and organization structure.
Use detail tables such as `m1_price_category_detail` and `m1_transaction_note_detail` when the user asks for row-level setup or source-specific content.
M1 is a master-data domain, not a staged transaction-document flow.
Avoid `custom*` fields unless they are explicitly requested by the user or required by a report.

query_patterns.name: master_listing
query_patterns.pattern: Use core tables such as `m1_contact`, `m1_item`, `m1_warehouse`, `m1_coa`, or `m1_branch` for master listings.

query_patterns.name: reference_lookup
query_patterns.pattern: Join primary master tables to categories, organization dimensions, or supporting references as needed.

query_patterns.name: item_classification_lookup
query_patterns.pattern: Use `m1_item` and then join to class-product, subdepartment, or selling-point references when needed.

query_patterns.name: coa_hierarchy_lookup
query_patterns.description: Account lookup and parent-child account hierarchy.
query_patterns.pattern: Use `m1_coa` and self-join on `cparent` when the user asks for account hierarchy.

query_patterns.name: transaction_note_lookup
query_patterns.pattern: Use `m1_transaction_note` and `m1_transaction_note_detail` with the `tnkode` and `tnsumber` pair.

caution_areas: Questions that mix contact master data with cross-domain business transactions.
Item questions that actually require inventory, purchasing, or sales transaction domains.
Account questions that really ask for transaction balances rather than account masters.
Questions that assume all contact categories live in a single table.
